title: Prove unbounded dyadic acquisition at rational rank one (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic obstruction with finite corroboration: rational rank one does not bound the number of eligible observations needed for a dyadic decoder. For every n>=1, the exact incremental acquisition count can be n. The prime-cover construction preserves every feasible selection and every positive weighted optimum of an arbitrary finite Set Cover instance.

```text
mandatory observation: (p_1 ... p_n) x
eligible observation i: (product_{j != i} p_j) x
allowed decoder coefficients: Z[1/2]
minimum additional acquisitions: n
rational observation rank throughout: 1
```

The three-entry fixture is `-105x + 2*35x + 21x + 15x = x`; every two-entry selection leaves an odd-prime obstruction. The proof is self-contained. Ali Romman #5789 supplies the rational-versus-dyadic question, cited rather than audited or replayed. Bezout, prime factorization, localization and weighted Set Cover are classical ingredients. No new complexity-theory classification or kappa is claimed.

## Evidence

- Before acquisition, the mandatory observation has a rational inverse but no dyadic inverse. After the complete singleton menu is acquired, constructed Bezout coefficients decode exactly. Each proper selection has a missing-prime obstruction.
- Warning-strict CPython 3.12.15 normal and optimized direct checks pass locally. Each registered command takes less than one second locally, below its 120-second limit. Registered replay and metadata checks pass.
- Complete finite checks cover 689 ordered menus, 5054 menu selections, 16609 weighted instances, 4530 literal scalar decodings and 8190 selections in the sharp family through n=12. All 15 rejection, four boundary and three semantic controls pass. Counts and SHA256 receipts are generated on stdout.
- Exact committed bytes and declared source-history preflight pass at `26309a3936985b3c7780856f708b0526508483bf`. The only Git-history source dependency is reachable base `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`. The pending predecessor is contextual, not an executable or mathematical dependency.

Reproduce from the repository root:

```sh
PY=/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12
"$PY" -W error -B research/sparse-dyadic-normalization/verify.py
"$PY" -W error -B -O research/sparse-dyadic-normalization/verify.py
"$PY" -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/sparse-dyadic-normalization
"$PY" -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/sparse-dyadic-normalization --check-source-history
```

Any CPython 3.12 interpreter can replace the local path. Expected markers are `PASS_SPARSE_DYADIC_NORMALIZATION`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. No third-party dependencies are used. The arbitrary-size theorem has a written proof; finite execution corroborates only its declared domain.

## Limitations

The menu is synthetic and its eligible observations are a declared interface. No current physical source is claimed to realize it. Observation production, coefficient preparation and growth, legal delivery, dirty restoration, native execution and the complete supplier bill remain unpriced. Adding an arbitrary observation such as x itself changes the problem. This is not a lower bound for unrestricted circuits, nonlinear decoding or a ring that inverts odd primes. The five framework assumptions and selected frontier are unchanged. No selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, rounded multiplier or independent proof-kernel validation was run.

## Open next questions

- Derive one nontrivial eligible prime-loss menu from a named physical producer/consumer cut, with complete acquisition and restoration charges.
- Prove a physical menu restriction, such as nested prime-loss sets or bounded incidence, that permits a bounded or tractable acquisition rule. Rational rank alone supplies no such restriction.

The package records first steps and blockers for both questions.

## Related open work

- #5789 provides rational rank and kernel certificates and excludes dyadic completion and physical delivery. This adds a sparse eligible-menu obstruction without changing or replaying that tool.
- #5882 studies dyadic unit-channel capacity under tensor composition. This fixes scalar rational rank one and minimizes acquired menu entries, a different objective and interface.
- #5889 studies dyadic feasibility of one supplied affine system with Smith charts and strict inequalities. This selects the observation system itself under acquisition charges and does not recompute its precision values.
- #5791 and #5878 study binary query-basis selection and partial acquisition dimensions. The odd-prime obstruction here uses Z[1/2] and asserts no agreement or disagreement with their binary values.
- #5903 computes constant-weight phase COPY approximation coefficients and leaves their Gaussian-dyadic realization open. This characterizes exact scalar acquisition over Z[1/2]; no approximation-error value is shared or compared.

The completion refresh inspected this account's eight other open PRs created since the CLAIM: #5897, #5898, #5899, #5900, #5901, #5902, #5903 and #5905. None computes a common scalar-menu acquisition value. No extra computations were run to validate their results.

The two errors are `KeyError: 'follow_up_steps'` and `KeyError: 'catalog_first_step'`. The assertion failures concern frozen-card/current-command routing, missing historical references and sparse omission behavior.

This matches the shared onboarding failure reported by the orchestrator for recent PRs based on main `de5ec2e7a`.
